The main takeaway from our work is that
transmembrane signaling by the insulin receptor is conserved to a remarkable degree in a receptor from a different organism that is not related to the insulin receptor by evolution.
transmembrane signaling is not a unique feature of the human insulin receptors, but is a conserved mechanism in other receptors.
transmembrane receptors share a common signaling mechanism, which can be used to generate new receptors with new properties.
